title: ArtibotTaskGraph
description: Structured Task Graph — canonical task state (design ARTIBOT-5.0-DESIGN.md §7.2 Addendum §7-8, which overrides v1 §3.5's 'state.yaml.workers is the worker source of truth'). The graph lives inside the StateStore; state.yaml.workers is a projection of it, never the reverse. No todo.md is created: the todo principle is kept, the file is not. Feeders are /split plan.json limbs (affectedPaths -> file_ownership) and /team TaskCreate.

schema_version.description: Migration handle required on every v5 artifact (design §7.2 Addendum §28-29).

mission_id.description: Owning mission; ids carry no repository prefix (design §7.2 Addendum §28-29). Two accepted forms, and BOTH must be accepted or the StateStore cannot join to the ledger: the issued form M-YYYYMMDD-NNN, with NNN free to run past three digits so a busy day cannot overflow the id space, and the session fallback M-YYYYMMDD-S<sid8> written when the substantive-mission gate declines to issue a mission. The same two forms are accepted by ledger-envelope.schema.json, review-output.schema.json and mission-contract.schema.json.

updated_at.description: ISO-8601 instant of the last graph mutation.

tasks.description: Task nodes. Node ids must be unique across the array and every dependency must name an existing node; neither is expressible in draft-07, so both stay a validator obligation of the StateStore (T-21), not of this schema. A consumer that trusts schema validity alone still has to check for duplicate ids and dangling dependencies.

blockerReason.description: Blocked reason convention from design §3.5 — lane:<x> | gate:<n> | human:<r> | reconcile:<w>. Written as an allowlist pattern on purpose: a deny-list would fail open for every prefix invented later.

evidenceRefs.description: References into the Evidence Registry (design §7.2 Addendum §23, .artibot/runtime/evidence.jsonl, ids shaped E-nnn). No id pattern is enforced here: the registry's id format is owned by the evidence-registry work, and pinning it from this schema would fork that contract.

id.description: Task identifier, unique within the graph (e.g. T-14, or a /split limb id).

mission_id.description: Owning mission; must equal the graph mission_id. Same two accepted forms as the graph-level field. Cross-field equality is a validator obligation, not a schema one.

status.description: The 8 canonical task states. The projection targets in design §3.5 (pending->queued, awaiting-dispatch->claimed, active/closing->executing, review->reviewing, serial-gate/suspended->blocked, done->done, plus the 9th 'failed' the ops vocabulary lacks) supply seven of them; 'cancelled' is the eighth added by design §7.2 Addendum §7-8. Mission status is a DIFFERENT vocabulary (see project-state.schema.json) and the two must not be merged.

owner.description: Worker/agent holding the task. Null or absent while queued.

dependencies.description: Ids of tasks that must reach a terminal state first. .plan-state.json had no dependency field; this is where dependency truth now lives.

blockers.description: Why this task cannot proceed, using the design §3.5 reason convention. The design names this vocabulary for the mission-level blocked_by; the same allowlist is applied here because it is the same vocabulary.

file_ownership.description: Path globs this task owns, fed by /split plan.json affectedPaths (design §7.2 Addendum §7-8). Coordination policy, not a Git lock (design §10). NOTE: §10's exclusive/read-only/unknown tri-state has no field of its own here — the design states the affectedPaths -> file_ownership mapping as a flat list and never gives the tri-state a shape, so none was invented.

retry_count.description: Attempts so far. Cost and retry accounting is per Run (design §8.2 §4·§42), so this is a coordination counter, not the economics record.

heartbeat_at.description: Last liveness signal. Null is the honest value today: the measured lane state has no heartbeat emitter (design §3.5). Until one exists the value is derived as max(lane-heartbeat, last-commit) and must carry heartbeat_source alongside (design §3.5).

heartbeat_source.description: Where heartbeat_at came from while it is a derived value — 'lane-heartbeat' or 'last-commit' per design §3.5. Required in spirit whenever heartbeat_at is derived rather than emitted; the schema cannot tell the two apart, so this stays optional.

verification.description: How this task is proven done. Accepts the plain command string that plan.json task entries already use, or an object when a result is recorded.

status.description: 'unmeasured' is a real state, not a default to hide: a leftover UNMEASURED blocks outcome.md generation (design §3.4).
